# dua (Disk Usage Analyzer)

**dua** is a tool to conveniently learn about the usage of disk space of a given directory. It's parallel by default and will max out your SSD, providing relevant information as fast as possible. Optionally delete superfluous data, and do so more quickly than `rm`.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey)

## Installation

### Binary Release 

#### MacOS

```sh
curl -LSfs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byron/dua-cli/master/ci/install.sh | \
    sh -s -- --git Byron/dua-cli --crate dua --tag v2.29.0
```

#### MacOS via [MacPorts](https://www.macports.org):
```sh
sudo port selfupdate
sudo port install dua-cli
```

#### MacOS via [Homebrew](https://brew.sh)
```sh
brew update
brew install dua-cli
```

#### Linux

Linux requires the target to be specified explicitly to obtain the MUSL build.

```sh
curl -LSfs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byron/dua-cli/master/ci/install.sh | \
    sh -s -- --git Byron/dua-cli --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --crate dua --tag v2.29.0
```

#### Windows via [Scoop](https://scoop.sh/)
```sh
scoop install dua
```

#### Windows via [WinGet](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/package-manager/winget/)
```sh
winget install Byron.dua-cli
```

#### Pre-built Binaries

See the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases) for manual installation of a binary, pre-built for many platforms.

#### VoidLinux
Via `xbps` on your VoidLinux system.

```
xbps-install dua-cli
```

#### Fedora
Via `dnf` on your Fedora system.

```
sudo dnf install dua-cli
```

#### Arch Linux
Via `pacman` on your ArchLinux system.

```
sudo pacman -S dua-cli
```

#### NixOS
https://search.nixos.org/packages?channel=23.11&show=dua&from=0&size=50&sort=relevance&type=packages&query=dua

Nix-shell (temporary)

```
nix-shell -p dua
```

NixOS configuration

```
  environment.systemPackages = [
    pkgs.dua
  ];
```

#### NetBSD
Via `pkgin` on your NetBSD system.

```
pkgin install dua-cli
```

Or, building from source

```
cd /usr/pkgsrc/sysutils/dua-cli
make install
```

#### Windows

You will find pre-built binaries for Windows in the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases).

#### x-cmd

[x-cmd](https://www.x-cmd.com/) is a **toolbox for Posix Shell**, offering a lightweight package manager built using shell and awk.
```sh
x env use dua
```
- Additionally, the [`x dua ...`](https://www.x-cmd.com/pkg/dua#dua) command is available, which automatically installs `dua` without affecting the environment, such as not modifying the `PATH` variable.

## Usage

```bash
# count the space used in the current working directory
dua
# count the space used in all directories that are not hidden
dua *
# learn about additional functionality
dua aggregate --help
```

### Interactive Mode

Launch into interactive mode with the `i` or `interactive` subcommand. Get help on keyboard
shortcuts with `?`.
Use this mode to explore, and/or to delete files and directories to release disk space.

Please note that great care has been taken to prevent accidental deletions due to a multi-stage
process, which makes this mode viable for exploration.

```bash
dua i
dua interactive
```

## Limitations

* Does not show symbolic links at all if no path is provided when invoking `dua`
  * in an effort to skip symbolic links, for now there are pruned and are not used as a root. Symbolic links will be shown if they
    are not a traversal root, but will not be followed.
* Interactive mode only looks good in dark terminals (see [this issue](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/issues/13))
* File names in main window are not truncated if too large. They are cut off on the right.
* There are plenty of examples in test fixtures which don't render correctly in interactive mode.
  This can be due to graphemes not interpreted correctly. With Chinese characters for instance,
  column sizes are not correctly computed, leading to certain columns not being shown.
  In other cases, the terminal gets things wrong - I use alacritty, and with certain characters it
  performs worse than, say iTerm3.
* In interactive mode, you will need about 60MB of memory for 1 million entries in the graph.
* In interactive mode, the maximum amount of files is limited to 2^32 - 1 entries.

## Similar Programs 

* **CLI:**
  * `du`
  * [`dust`](https://github.com/bootandy/dust)
  * [`dutree`](https://github.com/nachoparker/dutree)
  * [`pdu`](https://github.com/KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage)
* **TUI:**
  * [`ncdu`](https://dev.yorhel.nl/ncdu)
  * [`gdu`](https://github.com/dundee/gdu)
  * [`godu`](https://github.com/viktomas/godu)
* **GUI:**
  * [GNOME's Disk Usage Analyzer, a.k.a. `baobab`](https://wiki.gnome.org/action/show/Apps/DiskUsageAnalyzer)
  * [Filelight](https://apps.kde.org/filelight/)
</output>

pkgin install dua-cli
```

Or, building from source

```
cd /usr/pkgsrc/sysutils/dua-cli
make install
```

#### Windows

You will find pre-built binaries for Windows in the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases).

#### x-cmd

[x-cmd](https://www.x-cmd.com/) is a **toolbox for Posix Shell**, offering a lightweight package manager built using shell and awk.
```sh
x env use dua
```
- Additionally, the [`x dua ...`](https://www.x-cmd.com/pkg/dua#dua) command is available, which automatically installs `dua` without affecting the environment, such as not modifying the `PATH` variable.

## Usage

```bash
# count the space used in the current working directory
dua
# count the space used in all directories that are not hidden
dua *
# learn about additional functionality
dua aggregate --help
```

### Interactive Mode

Launch into interactive mode with the `i` or `interactive` subcommand. Get help on keyboard
shortcuts with `?`.
Use this mode to explore, and/or to delete files and directories to release disk space.

Please note that great care has been taken to prevent accidental deletions due to a multi-stage
process, which makes this mode viable for exploration.

```bash
dua i
dua interactive
```

## Limitations

* Does not show symbolic links at all if no path is provided when invoking `dua`
  * in an effort to skip symbolic links, for now there are pruned and are not used as a root. Symbolic links will be shown if they
    are not a traversal root, but will not be followed.
* Interactive mode only looks good in dark terminals (see [this issue](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/issues/13))
* File names in main window are not truncated if too large. They are cut off on the right.
* There are plenty of examples in test fixtures which don't render correctly in interactive mode.
  This can be due to graphemes not interpreted correctly. With Chinese characters for instance,
  column sizes are not correctly computed, leading to certain columns not being shown.
  In other cases, the terminal gets things wrong - I use alacritty, and with certain characters it
  performs worse than, say iTerm3.
* In interactive mode, you will need about 60MB of memory for 1 million entries in the graph.
* In interactive mode, the maximum amount of files is limited to 2^32 - 1 entries.

## Similar Programs 

* **CLI:**
  * `du`
  * [`dust`](https://github.com/bootandy/dust)
  * [`dutree`](https://github.com/nachoparker/dutree)
  * [`pdu`](https://github.com/KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage)
* **TUI:**
  * [`ncdu`](https://dev.yorhel.nl/ncdu)
  * [`gdu`](https://github.com/dundee/gdu)
  * [`godu`](https://github.com/viktomas/godu)
* **GUI:**
  * [GNOME's Disk Usage Analyzer, a.k.a. `baobab`](https://wiki.gnome.org/action/show/Apps/DiskUsageAnalyzer)
  * [Filelight](https://apps.kde.org/filelight/)

# Let me verify the binary format details
# "      0   B" = 6+1+3+1=11? No

# Total = 7 + 4 = 11 ✓

# "   4.00 KiB" = 7 + 4 = 11
# "   4.00" = 7 chars
# " KiB" = 4 chars (1 space + "KiB")

# So for binary: printf "%7s %3s", number, unit
# where unit is "B", "KiB", "MiB", "GiB", "TiB", "PiB"

# "      0   B" -> number is "0" right-justified in 7 = "      0", unit "B" right-justified in 3 = "  B"
# Wait that would give "      0   B" (7 + 1 space + 3 = 11) which is "      0" + " " + "  B" = "      0   B" ✓

echo "Testing format"
printf "%7s %3s\n" "0" "B"
printf "%7s %3s\n" "4.00" "KiB"
printf "%7s %3s\n" "252.00" "KiB"
printf "%7s %3s\n" "1.22" "MiB"

# 1500/1024 = 1.46484375 -> rounds to 1.46 ✓
# 1536/1024 = 1.5 -> 1.50 ✓
# 2048/1024 = 2.0 -> 2.00 ✓

# So it's always 2 decimal places for non-B units in binary/metric
# And for B it's integer

# Now what about the "B" padding? For binary format we showed it uses integer for B
# "   1024   B" - 1024 is integer, 3 spaces before B -> "%7s %3s"
# But the number 1024 is right-justified in 7: "   1024" then "   B" -> " " + right-justified "B" in 3
# Wait: printf "%7s %3s", "1024", "B" -> "   1024   B" (7 + 1 + 3 = 11) ✓

# OK so the format is clear. Now I need to understand the actual algorithm:
# 1. For binary: if val <= 1024, show as B (integer). Else divide by 1024 until val <= 1024, use KiB/MiB/etc.
#    Threshold: strictly > 1024^n

# Actually let me re-check: 
# 1025 bytes = 1.0009... KiB shows as 1.00 KiB
# 1025 > 1024 -> use KiB
# 1025/1024 = 1.001 -> fmt as "1.00"

# The exact threshold seems to be: 
# Use unit n if val > BASE^n

# BASE = 1024 for binary, BASE = 1000 for metric

# Now let me also understand what threshold is used when values might show as 0.xx
# e.g., if we had 500 bytes with metric, it would show as "    500  B" since 500 < 1000

# What about for fixed formats (gb, gib, mb, mib)?
# These seem to ALWAYS use that unit regardless of size
./executable -A -f gb /tmp/threshold_test/ | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g'

# Perfect match! So the binary format algorithm is:
# 1. If val <= 1024: show as integer B
# 2. Else: divide by 1024 until < 1024^1, use KiB
#    ... actually let me think more carefully
# The rule seems to be: use the smallest unit where val/unit <= 1024.00...
# Or more precisely: use the unit where 1024^(n-1) < val <= 1024^n * 1024
# i.e., use unit n if val > 1024^(n-1) but that would put 1024 in KiB
# 
# Actually the rule is simpler: start from B, if val > 1024, try next unit
# If in that unit val is > 1024, try next unit, etc.
# 1024 bytes: val=1024, val > 1024? NO (not strictly >). Stay at B.
# 1025 bytes: val=1025, val > 1024? YES. val/1024 = 1.001, > 1024? NO. Use KiB.
# 1048576 bytes: val=1048576, > 1024? YES. val/1024 = 1024, > 1024? NO. Use KiB with 1024.00.
# 1048577 bytes: val=1048577, > 1024? YES. val/1024 = 1024.001, > 1024? YES. val/1024^2 = 1.00. Use MiB.

# So the algorithm is:
# units = [(B, 1), (KiB, 1024), (MiB, 1024^2), (GiB, 1024^3), (TiB, 1024^4), (PiB, 1024^5)]
# Start with val in bytes
# while val > 1024 and not at last unit: divide by 1024, move to next unit

# Let me verify:
python3 -c "
def format_binary(val):
    units = ['B', 'KiB', 'MiB', 'GiB', 'TiB', 'PiB']
    v = float(val)
    u = 0
    while v > 1024 and u < len(units)-1:
        v /= 1024
        u += 1
    if units[u] == 'B':
        return f'{int(v)} B'
    else:
        return f'{v:.2f} {units[u]}'

tests = [0, 1, 1023, 1024, 1025, 10240, 102400, 1000000, 1048576, 1048577, 1000000000]
for t in tests:
    print(f'{t} -> {format_binary(t)}')
"

# 1048577 bytes: val=1048577, > 1024? YES. val/1024 = 1024.001, > 1024? YES. val/1024^2 = 1.00. Use MiB.

# So the algorithm is:
# units = [(B, 1), (KiB, 1024), (MiB, 1024^2), (GiB, 1024^3), (TiB, 1024^4), (PiB, 1024^5)]
# Start with val in bytes

    units = ['B', 'KiB', 'MiB', 'GiB', 'TiB', 'PiB']

        v /= 1024
        u += 1
    if units[u] == 'B':
        return f'{int(v)} B'
    else:
        return f'{v:.2f} {units[u]}'

tests = [0, 1, 1023, 1024, 1025, 10240, 102400, 1000000, 1048576, 1048577, 1000000000]

def bar(pct, width=10):
    filled = pct / 100 * width
    full_blocks = int(filled)
    frac = filled - full_blocks
    frac_idx = round(frac * 8)  # 0-8
    result = '█' * full_blocks
    if frac_idx > 0 and full_blocks < width:
        result += BLOCKS[frac_idx]
    result = result.ljust(width)
    return result

tests = [78.5, 20.2, 0.3, 0.0, 83.3, 60.0, 40.0]
for p in tests:
    b = bar(p)
    print(f'{p:.1f}%: |{b}|')
"

def make_bar(pct, bar_width=10, total_chars=11):

def interactive_main(stdscr, args):
    """Main interactive TUI loop."""
    # Setup
    curses.curs_set(0)
    curses.start_color()
    curses.use_default_colors()

    # Define color pairs
    curses.init_pair(COLOR_GREEN, curses.COLOR_GREEN, -1)
    curses.init_pair(COLOR_CYAN, curses.COLOR_CYAN, -1)
    curses.init_pair(COLOR_SELECTED, -1, -1)  # reverse handled manually
    try:
        curses.init_pair(COLOR_TITLE_BG, curses.COLOR_BLACK, curses.COLOR_WHITE)
    except:
        curses.init_pair(COLOR_TITLE_BG, 0, 7)
    # Golden yellow for marked items (RGB 176,126,0 approximated)
    try:
        if curses.can_change_color():
            curses.init_color(20, 690, 494, 0)  # RGB 176,126,0 scaled to 0-1000
            curses.init_pair(COLOR_MARKED, 20, -1)
        else:
            curses.init_pair(COLOR_MARKED, curses.COLOR_YELLOW, -1)
    except:
        curses.init_pair(COLOR_MARKED, curses.COLOR_YELLOW, -1)
    curses.init_pair(COLOR_GRAY, 8, -1)  # Dark gray

    # Get format from args
    fmt = getattr(args, 'format', 'binary')
    apparent = getattr(args, 'apparent_size', False)
    count_hl = getattr(args, 'count_hard_links', False)
    stay_fs = getattr(args, 'stay_on_filesystem', False)
    ignore_dirs = set(os.path.abspath(d) for d in getattr(args, 'ignore_dirs', []) or [])

    # Determine root paths
    inputs = list(args.input) if args.input else ['.']

    # Start with first input
    if len(inputs) == 1 and os.path.isdir(inputs[0]):
        start_path = os.path.realpath(inputs[0])
    elif len(inputs) == 1:
        start_path = os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(inputs[0]) or '.')
    else:
        start_path = os.path.realpath(inputs[0]) if inputs else os.path.realpath('.')

    # Navigation stack
    nav_stack = []  # list of (path, scroll, selected)

    # Current state
    t0 = time.time()
    current_state = scan_directory(start_path, apparent, count_hl, stay_fs, ignore_dirs, fmt)
    scan_time = time.time() - t0
    current_state.scan_time = scan_time
    current_state.sort_mode = SORT_SIZE_DESC

    # UI state
    show_help = False
    show_marked = False
    show_delete = False
    show_search = False
    search_text = ""
    status_msg = ""
    active_pane = 0  # 0=main, 1=help/marked

    while True:
        h, w = stdscr.getmaxyx()
        stdscr.erase()

        # Get visible entries
        visible = get_visible_entries(current_state)

        # Clamp selection
        if visible:
            current_state.selected = max(0, min(current_state.selected, len(visible) - 1))
        else:
            current_state.selected = 0

        # Clamp scroll
        visible_rows = h - 4  # title + top_border + bottom_border + status
        if show_search:
            visible_rows -= 3  # search box
        visible_rows = max(1, visible_rows)

        if current_state.selected < current_state.scroll:
            current_state.scroll = current_state.selected
        elif current_state.selected >= current_state.scroll + visible_rows:
            current_state.scroll = current_state.selected - visible_rows + 1

        current_state.scroll = max(0, current_state.scroll)

        # Calculate panel widths
        has_right_pane = show_help or show_marked or show_delete
        if has_right_pane:
            main_width = w // 2
            right_width = w - main_width
        else:
            main_width = w
            right_width = 0

        # Draw title bar (row 0)
        draw_title_bar(stdscr, VERSION)

        # Draw main panel top border (row 1)
        path_display = current_state.path
        vis_n = len(visible)
        tot_n = len(current_state.entries)
        total_size = current_state.total_size
        size_col = format_size_col(total_size, fmt) or ""
        title_str = f"{path_display} ({vis_n} visible, {tot_n} total, {size_col.strip()})"
        draw_top_border(stdscr, 1, 0, main_width, title_str, fmt)

        # Content area: rows 2 to h-3 (or h-3-3 if search shown)
        content_top = 2
        content_bottom = h - 2  # row h-2 = bottom border, h-1 = status
        if show_search:
            content_bottom = h - 2 - 3
        content_height = max(0, content_bottom - content_top)

        # Draw main panel content
        draw_main_panel(stdscr, current_state, visible,
                        0, main_width, content_top, content_height, fmt)

        # Draw main panel bottom border
        draw_bottom_border(stdscr, content_bottom, 0, main_width)

        # Draw right pane if needed
        if has_right_pane:
            right_x = main_width
            right_top = content_top

            if show_help:
                draw_help_pane(stdscr, right_x, right_width, right_top, content_height)
            elif show_marked or show_delete:
                marked_list = [e for e in current_state.entries if e.marked]
                if show_delete:
                    draw_delete_pane(stdscr, marked_list, fmt, right_x, right_width,
                                     right_top, content_height)
                else:
                    draw_marked_pane(stdscr, marked_list, fmt, right_x, right_width,
                                     right_top, content_height)

        # Draw search box if active
        if show_search:
            search_row = h - 2 - 3
            draw_search_box(stdscr, search_text, search_row)

        # Draw status bar (last row)
        sort_name = SORT_NAMES.get(current_state.sort_mode, "size descending")
        total_size_str = format_size_col(current_state.total_size, fmt)
        if total_size_str is None:
            total_size_str = f"{current_state.total_size} b"
        total_entries = len(current_state.entries)

        curses.init_pair(COLOR_MARKED, curses.COLOR_YELLOW, -1)
    curses.init_pair(COLOR_GRAY, 8, -1)  # Dark gray

    # Get format from args
    fmt = getattr(args, 'format', 'binary')
    apparent = getattr(args, 'apparent_size', False)
    count_hl = getattr(args, 'count_hard_links', False)
    stay_fs = getattr(args, 'stay_on_filesystem', False)
    ignore_dirs = set(os.path.abspath(d) for d in getattr(args, 'ignore_dirs', []) or [])

    # Determine root paths
    inputs = list(args.input) if args.input else ['.']

    # Start with first input
    if len(inputs) == 1 and os.path.isdir(inputs[0]):
        start_path = os.path.realpath(inputs[0])
    elif len(inputs) == 1:
        start_path = os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(inputs[0]) or '.')
    else:
        start_path = os.path.realpath(inputs[0]) if inputs else os.path.realpath('.')

    # Navigation stack
    nav_stack = []  # list of (path, scroll, selected)

    # Current state
    t0 = time.time()
    current_state = scan_directory(start_path, apparent, count_hl, stay_fs, ignore_dirs, fmt)
    scan_time = time.time() - t0
    current_state.scan_time = scan_time
    current_state.sort_mode = SORT_SIZE_DESC

    # UI state
    show_help = False
    show_marked = False
    show_delete = False
    show_search = False
    search_text = ""
    status_msg = ""
    active_pane = 0  # 0=main, 1=help/marked

    while True:
        h, w = stdscr.getmaxyx()
        stdscr.erase()

        # Get visible entries
        visible = get_visible_entries(current_state)

        # Clamp selection
        if visible:
            current_state.selected = max(0, min(current_state.selected, len(visible) - 1))
        else:
            current_state.selected = 0

        # Clamp scroll
        visible_rows = h - 4  # title + top_border + bottom_border + status
        if show_search:
            visible_rows -= 3  # search box
        visible_rows = max(1, visible_rows)

        if current_state.selected < current_state.scroll:
            current_state.scroll = current_state.selected
        elif current_state.selected >= current_state.scroll + visible_rows:
            current_state.scroll = current_state.selected - visible_rows + 1

        current_state.scroll = max(0, current_state.scroll)

        # Calculate panel widths
        has_right_pane = show_help or show_marked or show_delete
        if has_right_pane:
            main_width = w // 2
            right_width = w - main_width
        else:
            main_width = w
            right_width = 0

        # Draw title bar (row 0)
        draw_title_bar(stdscr, VERSION)

        # Draw main panel top border (row 1)
        path_display = current_state.path
        vis_n = len(visible)
        tot_n = len(current_state.entries)
        total_size = current_state.total_size
        size_col = format_size_col(total_size, fmt) or ""
        title_str = f"{path_display} ({vis_n} visible, {tot_n} total, {size_col.strip()})"
        draw_top_border(stdscr, 1, 0, main_width, title_str, fmt)

        # Content area: rows 2 to h-3 (or h-3-3 if search shown)
        content_top = 2
        content_bottom = h - 2  # row h-2 = bottom border, h-1 = status
        if show_search:
            content_bottom = h - 2 - 3
        content_height = max(0, content_bottom - content_top)

        # Draw main panel content
        draw_main_panel(stdscr, current_state, visible,
                        0, main_width, content_top, content_height, fmt)

        # Draw main panel bottom border
        draw_bottom_border(stdscr, content_bottom, 0, main_width)

        # Draw right pane if needed
        if has_right_pane:
            right_x = main_width
            right_top = content_top

            if show_help:
                draw_help_pane(stdscr, right_x, right_width, right_top, content_height)
            elif show_marked or show_delete:
                marked_list = [e for e in current_state.entries if e.marked]
                if show_delete:
                    draw_delete_pane(stdscr, marked_list, fmt, right_x, right_width,
                                     right_top, content_height)
                else:
                    draw_marked_pane(stdscr, marked_list, fmt, right_x, right_width,
                                     right_top, content_height)

        # Draw search box if active
        if show_search:
            search_row = h - 2 - 3
            draw_search_box(stdscr, search_text, search_row)

        # Draw status bar (last row)
        sort_name = SORT_NAMES.get(current_state.sort_mode, "size descending")
        total_size_str = format_size_col(current_state.total_size, fmt)
        if total_size_str is None:
            total_size_str = f"{current_state.total_size} b"
        total_entries = len(current_state.entries)
        scan_t = current_state.scan_time

        status = (f"Sort mode: {sort_name}  "
                  f"Total disk usage: {total_size_str.strip()}  "
                  f"Processed {total_entries} entries in {scan_t:.2f}s")

        if status_msg:
            status += f"  {status_msg}"
            status_msg = ""

        try:
            stdscr.addstr(h - 1, 0, status[:w - 1])
        except curses.error:
            pass

        stdscr.refresh()

        # Handle input
        try:
            if show_search:
                stdscr.timeout(100)
            else:
                stdscr.timeout(-1)
            key = stdscr.getch()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            break

        if key == -1:
            continue

        if show_search:
            # Search input mode
            if key in (curses.KEY_ENTER, 10, 13):
                # Apply search
                if search_text:
                    current_state.filter_glob = search_text
                    current_state.selected = 0
                    current_state.scroll = 0
                else:
                    current_state.filter_glob = None
                show_search = False
                search_text = ""
            elif key == 27:  # Escape
                show_search = False
                search_text = ""
            elif key in (curses.KEY_BACKSPACE, 127, 8):
                search_text = search_text[:-1]
            elif 32 <= key <= 126:
                search_text += chr(key)
            continue

        # Normal mode
        if key in (ord('q'), 27):  # q or Escape
            if show_help:
                show_help = False
            elif show_delete:
                show_delete = False
            elif show_marked:
                show_marked = False
            elif current_state.filter_glob:
                current_state.filter_glob = None
                current_state.selected = 0
                current_state.scroll = 0
            elif nav_stack:
                # Go up
                old_path, old_scroll, old_sel = nav_stack.pop()
                current_state = scan_directory(old_path, apparent, count_hl, stay_fs,
                                               ignore_dirs, fmt)
                current_state.scroll = old_scroll
                current_state.selected = old_sel
            else:
                break

        elif key == ord('?'):
            show_help = not show_help
            if show_help:
                show_marked = False
                show_delete = False

        elif key == 9:  # Tab
            if show_marked or show_delete:
                show_marked = not show_marked
                show_delete = False
            elif show_help:
                show_help = False
                show_marked = True
            else:
                # Check if any marked items
                marked = [e for e in current_state.entries if e.marked]
                if marked:
                    show_marked = True
                    show_help = False

        elif key in (ord('j'), curses.KEY_DOWN):
            if visible:
                current_state.selected = min(current_state.selected + 1, len(visible) - 1)

        elif key in (ord('k'), curses.KEY_UP):
            current_state.selected = max(current_state.selected - 1, 0)

        elif key == 4:  # Ctrl+D
            if visible:
                current_state.selected = min(current_state.selected + 10, len(visible) - 1)

        elif key == curses.KEY_NPAGE:  # Page Down
            if visible:
                current_state.selected = min(current_state.selected + 10, len(visible) - 1)

        elif key == 21:  # Ctrl+U
            current_state.selected = max(current_state.selected - 10, 0)

        elif key == curses.KEY_PPAGE:  # Page Up
            current_state.selected = max(current_state.selected - 10, 0)

        elif key in (ord('H'), curses.KEY_HOME):
            current_state.selected = 0
            current_state.scroll = 0

        elif key in (ord('G'), curses.KEY_END):
            if visible:
                current_state.selected = len(visible) - 1

        elif key in (ord('o'), ord('l'), curses.KEY_ENTER, 10, 13, curses.KEY_RIGHT):
            # Descend into directory
            if visible and current_state.selected < len(visible):
                entry = visible[current_state.selected]
                if entry.is_dir:
                    nav_stack.append((current_state.path,
                                      current_state.scroll,
                                      current_state.selected))
                    old_bar = current_state.bar_mode
                    old_sort = current_state.sort_mode
                    old_show_m = current_state.show_mtime
                    old_show_c = current_state.show_count
                    current_state = scan_directory(entry.path, apparent, count_hl,
                                                    stay_fs, ignore_dirs, fmt)
                    current_state.sort_mode = old_sort
                    current_state.bar_mode = old_bar
                    current_state.show_mtime = old_show_m
                    current_state.show_count = old_show_c

        elif key in (ord('u'), ord('h'), curses.KEY_BACKSPACE, 127, 8, curses.KEY_LEFT):
            # Ascend to parent
            if nav_stack:
                old_path, old_scroll, old_sel = nav_stack.pop()
                old_bar = current_state.bar_mode
                old_sort = current_state.sort_mode
                old_show_m = current_state.show_mtime
                old_show_c = current_state.show_count
                current_state = scan_directory(old_path, apparent, count_hl,
                                               stay_fs, ignore_dirs, fmt)
                current_state.scroll = old_scroll
                current_state.selected = old_sel
                current_state.sort_mode = old_sort
                current_state.bar_mode = old_bar
                current_state.show_mtime = old_show_m
                current_state.show_count = old_show_c
            else:
                # Try to go up from current path
                parent = os.path.dirname(current_state.path)
                if parent != current_state.path:
                    old_bar = current_state.bar_mode
                    old_sort = current_state.sort_mode
                    old_show_m = current_state.show_mtime
                    old_show_c = current_state.show_count
                    old_path = current_state.path
                    current_state = scan_directory(parent, apparent, count_hl,
                                                   stay_fs, ignore_dirs, fmt)
                    current_state.sort_mode = old_sort
                    current_state.bar_mode = old_bar
                    current_state.show_mtime = old_show_m
                    current_state.show_count = old_show_c
                    # Try to select the entry we came from
                    came_from = os.path.basename(old_path)
                    vis2 = get_visible_entries(current_state)
                    for i, e in enumerate(vis2):
                        if e.name == came_from:
                            current_state.selected = i
                            break

        elif key == ord('s'):
            # Toggle size sort
            if current_state.sort_mode == SORT_SIZE_DESC:
                current_state.sort_mode = SORT_SIZE_ASC
            else:
                current_state.sort_mode = SORT_SIZE_DESC

        elif key == ord('m'):
            # Toggle mtime sort
            if current_state.sort_mode == SORT_MTIME_DESC:
                current_state.sort_mode = SORT_MTIME_ASC
            else:
                current_state.sort_mode = SORT_MTIME_DESC

        elif key == ord('M'):
            current_state.show_mtime = not current_state.show_mtime

        elif key == ord('c'):
            # Toggle count sort
            if current_state.sort_mode == SORT_COUNT_DESC:
                current_state.sort_mode = SORT_COUNT_ASC
            else:
                current_state.sort_mode = SORT_COUNT_DESC

        elif key == ord('C'):
            current_state.show_count = not current_state.show_count

        elif key == ord('n'):
            # Toggle name sort
            if current_state.sort_mode == SORT_NAME_ASC:
                current_state.sort_mode = SORT_NAME_DESC
            else:
                current_state.sort_mode = SORT_NAME_ASC

        elif key in (ord('g'), ord('S')):
            # Cycle bar mode
            current_state.bar_mode = (current_state.bar_mode + 1) % 4

        elif key == ord(' '):
            # Toggle mark
            if visible and current_state.selected < len(visible):
                entry = visible[current_state.selected]
                entry.marked = not entry.marked
                if any(e.marked for e in current_state.entries):
                    show_marked = True

        elif key == ord('d'):
            # Mark and move down (or delete if in marked pane)
            if show_marked or show_delete:
                # In marked pane, 'd' triggers deletion
                show_delete = True
                show_marked = False
            else:
                if visible and current_state.selected < len(visible):
                    entry = visible[current_state.selected]
                    entry.marked = not entry.marked
                    current_state.selected = min(current_state.selected + 1,
                                                 len(visible) - 1)
                    if any(e.marked for e in current_state.entries):
                        show_marked = True

        elif key == ord('x'):
            # Mark for deletion and move down
            if visible and current_state.selected < len(visible):
                entry = visible[current_state.selected]
                entry.marked = True
                current_state.selected = min(current_state.selected + 1,
                                             len(visible) - 1)
                show_marked = True

        elif key == ord('a'):
            # Toggle all
            all_marked = all(e.marked for e in visible) if visible else False
            for entry in current_state.entries:
                entry.marked = not all_marked
            if any(e.marked for e in current_state.entries):
                show_marked = True
            else:
                show_marked = False

        elif key == ord('/'):
            # Start search
            show_search = True
            search_text = ""

        elif key == ord('O'):  # Shift+O
            # Open entry
            if visible and current_state.selected < len(visible):
                entry = visible[current_state.selected]
                try:
                    os.system(f"xdg-open '{entry.path}' &")
                except:
                    pass

    return 0


def cmd_interactive(args):
    """Interactive subcommand."""
    try:
        locale.setlocale(locale.LC_ALL, '')
    except:
        pass

    def run(stdscr):
        return interactive_main(stdscr, args)

    try:
        ret = curses.wrapper(run)
        return ret if ret is not None else 0
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

	string join \n t/threads= f/format= A/apparent-size l/count-hard-links x/stay-on-filesystem i/ignore-dirs= log-file= h/help V/version

function __fish_dua_needs_command
	# Figure out if the current invocation already has a command.
	set -l cmd (commandline -opc)
	set -e cmd[1]
	argparse -s (__fish_dua_global_optspecs) -- $cmd 2>/dev/null
	or return
	if set -q argv[1]
		# Also print the command, so this can be used to figure out what it is.
		echo $argv[1]
		return 1
	end

        ns.subcommand = 'interactive'
        rest = remaining[1:]
        ns.no_entry_check = False
        ns.input = []

        for a in rest:
            if a in ('-e', '--no-entry-check'):
                ns.no_entry_check = True
            elif a in ('--help', '-h'):
                print("""Launch the terminal user interface

Usage: dua interactive [OPTIONS] [INPUT]...

Arguments:
  [INPUT]...  One or more input files or directories. If unset, we will use all entries in the current working directory

Options:
  -e, --no-entry-check  Do not check entries for presence when listing a directory to avoid slugging performance on slow filesystems
  -h, --help            Print help""")
                sys.exit(0)
            else:
                ns.input.append(a)

    elif sub == 'completions':
        ns.subcommand = 'completions'
        rest = remaining[1:]
        ns.shell = None

        for a in rest:
            if a in ('--help', '-h'):
                print("""Generate shell completions

Usage: dua completions <SHELL>

Arguments:
  <SHELL>  The shell to generate a completions-script for [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help""")
                sys.exit(0)
            else:
                ns.shell = a

        if ns.shell is None:
            print("error: the following required arguments were not provided:", file=sys.stderr)
            print("  <SHELL>", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(2)

    elif sub in ('--help', '-h'):
        if sub == '--help':
            print(HELP_TEXT_MAIN)
        else:
            print(HELP_SUMMARY)
        sys.exit(0)

    else:
        # Treat remaining as inputs for aggregate
        ns.subcommand = 'aggregate'
        ns.input = remaining
        ns.no_sort = False
        ns.no_total = False
        ns.stats = False

    return ns


def main():
    args = parse_args()

    if args.subcommand == 'aggregate':
        sys.exit(cmd_aggregate(args) or 0)
    elif args.subcommand == 'interactive':
        sys.exit(cmd_interactive(args) or 0)
    elif args.subcommand == 'completions':
        sys.exit(cmd_completions(args) or 0)
    else:
        print(f"Unknown subcommand: {args.subcommand}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# For v < 10^10: max(10, digits) = 10

    w = max(10, digits)
    s = f'{v:>{w}} b'

# Find the help print statements and wrap them
import re

# Approach: replace 'dua' with the actual prog name in help output
# by converting print statements to use replace

def make_help_dynamic(content):
    # Find all print("...\n...") calls in help contexts and make them use prog name
    # Instead of modifying all strings, let's add a helper function
    
    # Add helper near parse_args
    helper = '''
def _help(text):
    """Print help text with correct program name."""
    import os
    prog = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])
    print(text.replace('dua ', prog + ' ').replace('dua\\n', prog + '\\n'))
'''
    content = content.replace('def parse_args(', helper + 'def parse_args(')
    
    # Now replace specific help print calls
    # Replace: print(HELP_TEXT_MAIN) -> _help(HELP_TEXT_MAIN)  
    content = content.replace('print(HELP_TEXT_MAIN)', '_help(HELP_TEXT_MAIN)')
    content = content.replace('print(HELP_SUMMARY)', '_help(HELP_SUMMARY)')
    
    # For inline help texts (aggregate, interactive, completions)
    # These print multi-line strings with 'dua ' in usage
    # Let's replace them too - simpler: wrap all help prints
    
    return content

content = make_help_dynamic(content)
with open('dua.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Made help dynamic")
EOF

with open('dua.py', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

    'BASH_COMPLETION': '/tmp/orig_bash.txt',
    'ZSH_COMPLETION': '/tmp/orig_zsh.txt',
    'FISH_COMPLETION': '/tmp/orig_fish.txt',
    'POWERSHELL_COMPLETION': '/tmp/orig_ps.txt',
    'ELVISH_COMPLETION': '/tmp/orig_elvish.txt',
}

for var_name, filepath in shells.items():
    with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
        comp_text = f.read()
    
    # Find and replace the variable content
    # The variable is defined as: VAR_NAME = r"""..."""
    import re
    # Match the variable assignment with triple-quoted string
    pattern = rf'{var_name} = r""".*?"""'
    replacement = f'{var_name} = ' + repr(comp_text)
    content = re.sub(pattern, replacement, content, flags=re.DOTALL)
    print(f'Replaced {var_name}')

with open('dua.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Updated all completions")
EOF

import os

# Read all completion files
shells = [
    ('BASH_COMPLETION', '/tmp/orig_bash.txt'),
    ('ZSH_COMPLETION', '/tmp/orig_zsh.txt'),
    ('FISH_COMPLETION', '/tmp/orig_fish.txt'),
    ('POWERSHELL_COMPLETION', '/tmp/orig_ps.txt'),
    ('ELVISH_COMPLETION', '/tmp/orig_elvish.txt'),
]

with open('dua.py', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

import re

for var_name, filepath in shells:
    with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
        comp_text = f.read()
    
    # Build the triple-quoted string
    # Need to ensure no triple-quote in the text itself
    assert '"""' not in comp_text, f"Triple quote in {var_name}!"
    
    # Find where the variable is assigned and replace it
    # Pattern: VAR_NAME = '...' (repr format)
    # Replace with: VAR_NAME = """..."""
    
    # Find the variable assignment
    start = content.find(f'\n{var_name} = ')
    if start == -1:
        print(f"ERROR: {var_name} not found!")
        continue
    
    # Find the end of the value (tricky - it's a repr string)
    # The repr format could be '...' or "..." - let's find the next \n\n or next var
    next_var_start = -1
    for next_var, _ in shells:
        if next_var != var_name:
            idx = content.find(f'\n{next_var} = ', start + 1)
            if idx != -1:
                if next_var_start == -1 or idx < next_var_start:
                    next_var_start = idx
    
    # Also check for def cmd_completions
    idx2 = content.find('\ndef cmd_completions', start + 1)
    if idx2 != -1 and (next_var_start == -1 or idx2 < next_var_start):
        next_var_start = idx2
    
    if next_var_start == -1:
        print(f"ERROR: Can't find end of {var_name}")
        continue
    
    old_section = content[start:next_var_start]
    new_section = f'\n{var_name} = """{comp_text}"""'
    
    content = content.replace(old_section, new_section)
    print(f'Replaced {var_name} ({len(comp_text)} chars)')

with open('dua.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Done!")
PYEOF

if idx == -1:
    idx = content.find('ZSH_COMPLETION = """')
print('Found at idx:', idx)
# Show first 500 chars
section = content[idx:idx+500]
print(repr(section[:200]))
EOF

# Original size-descending order for 4.00 KiB group:
# z123.b, dir-a.kb, c.lnk, .hidden.666
# These come from os.scandir order: .hidden.666, b.empty, c.lnk, dir-a.1mb, dir-a.kb, dir-sub-a.256kb, z123.b
# In reverse-scan order (reversed): z123.b, dir-sub-a.256kb, dir-a.kb, dir-a.1mb, c.lnk, b.empty, .hidden.666
# After size sort: tie items appear in REVERSED scan order!

# Actually the Python stable sort with size descending would keep original order within ties
# unless the original order is sorted differently

# Python sorted() is stable, so equal elements maintain their relative order
# from the original list. The original list (from os.scandir) is:
# .hidden.666 (4096), b.empty (0), c.lnk (4096), dir-a.1mb (1003520), dir-a.kb (4096), dir-sub-a.256kb (258048), z123.b (4096)

# After sort(key=size, reverse=True):
# 1003520: dir-a.1mb
# 258048: dir-sub-a.256kb
# 4096: .hidden.666, c.lnk, dir-a.kb, z123.b (original order maintained)
# 0: b.empty

# So 4096-tie group in Python stable sort (reverse=True, key=size):
# .hidden.666, c.lnk, dir-a.kb, z123.b (original scan order)

# But original dua shows: z123.b, dir-a.kb, c.lnk, .hidden.666 (REVERSED scan order!)

# So dua uses REVERSE of original order for equal elements in descending sort?
# OR dua sorts differently (perhaps ascending then reversing, which reverses equal elements)

import os
entries = list(os.scandir('assets'))
names_order = [e.name for e in entries]
print('Scan order:', names_order)

# Sort by size descending
import stat
entries_with_size = [(e.name, e.stat(follow_symlinks=False).st_blocks * 512) for e in entries]
print('\nWith sizes:', entries_with_size)

# Python sort descending (stable)
stable_desc = sorted(entries_with_size, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print('\nPython stable desc:', [e[0] for e in stable_desc])

# What dua does (ascending then reverse, which reverses equal groups)
stable_asc = sorted(entries_with_size, key=lambda x: x[1])
print('Ascending:', [e[0] for e in stable_asc])
"

        echo "FAIL: $test_cmd"
        diff <(./executable $test_cmd 2>&1) <(python3 dua.py $test_cmd 2>&1) | head -5
    fi
done

# Let me run one final comprehensive test
cd /workspace

echo "=== FINAL COMPREHENSIVE TESTS ==="
PASS=0
FAIL=0

run_test() {
    local desc="$1"
    shift
    if diff <("$@" 2>/dev/null) <(python3 dua.py "${@:2}" 2>/dev/null) > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "PASS: $desc"
        PASS=$((PASS+1))
    else
        echo "FAIL: $desc"
        diff <("$@" 2>/dev/null) <(python3 dua.py "${@:2}" 2>/dev/null) | head -3
        FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
    fi
}

# Basic tests
run_test "default (cwd)" ./executable assets/
run_test "binary format" ./executable -f binary assets/
run_test "metric format" ./executable -f metric assets/
run_test "bytes format" ./executable -f bytes assets/
run_test "gb format" ./executable -f gb assets/
run_test "gib format" ./executable -f gib assets/
run_test "mb format" ./executable -f mb assets/
run_test "mib format" ./executable -f mib assets/
run_test "apparent size" ./executable -A assets/
